concerns.concern: The headline claim rests on effective conductivity alone. A power-factor comparison with conventional Pt/YIG devices is missing, and a rough estimate suggests no net gain because the higher conductivity is offset by a roughly 10× lower Seebeck coefficient. Claims of significant improvement should be tempered and a literature table and in-house reference added.
concerns.quote: The ~10–100× gain in σ_eff appears to be largely cancelled by a ~10× lower S.

concerns.concern: There is no nonmagnetic-core control: Pt-coated nonmagnetic insulating powders processed identically. This would capture field-odd signals from the Pt network, Fe-doped Pt or contamination.
concerns.quote: This is the single most important missing experiment.

concerns.concern: The two measurement configurations are symmetry-equivalent for an isotropic medium. Their agreement shows only macroscopic isotropy, not an SSE origin, since a dispersed ferromagnetic-metal ANE would be equally isotropic, yet the Results present it as SSE evidence.
concerns.quote: Agreement between them demonstrates macroscopic isotropy of the pellet, not the SSE origin.

concerns.concern: Co-bonded WC tooling and crushing tools could introduce Co/Fe debris during high-pressure pressing. An impurity check by ICP/EDX is needed.
concerns.quote: Pressing at 500 MPa could plausibly transfer Co/Fe debris.

concerns.concern: No spin-Hall-angle control was done. Coating YIG with W or Ta should reverse the signal sign, and coating with Cu should suppress it.
concerns.quote: A sign reversal would be close to a smoking gun.

concerns.concern: The XRD argument against impurity phases is weak. Detection limits are far above impurity levels that could produce the observed signal, and key Fe₃O₄ and FePt peaks overlap YIG and Pt reflections.
concerns.quote: "No detectable peaks" therefore says little.

concerns.concern: A decreased saturation magnetization does not rule out ferromagnetic secondary phases. A percent-level Fe₃O₄ inclusion would be masked by dilution.
concerns.quote: The logic that "Ms decreased, so no ferromagnetic secondary phases" does not hold.

concerns.concern: The ~25% drop in Ms is unexplained. It is the same for 15 and 30 nm Pt and too large for dilution, possibly indicating dead surface layers, interfacial reaction or normalization errors.
concerns.quote: More importantly, the observed decrease is itself unexplained

concerns.concern: The Hall measurement is not quantified. The authors should fit linear plus saturating terms, give an upper bound on any anomalous Hall component, and convert it into an upper bound on possible ANE.
concerns.quote: This is the strongest of the three arguments but is not quantified

concerns.concern: Spin-Hall-magnetoresistance-type Hall terms at randomly oriented Pt/YIG interfaces would also give a magnetization-proportional Hall contribution. This needs discussion.
concerns.quote: spin-Hall-magnetoresistance-type Hall terms at randomly oriented Pt/YIG interfaces would also give an M-proportional Hall contribution

concerns.concern: The field dependence of the signal should be overlaid with M(H), demagnetization-corrected, in the same orientation. The differing saturation fields in Fig. 3b and Fig. 3e need explanation.
concerns.quote: The saturation fields in Fig. 3b (~1–2 kOe) and Fig. 3e (apparently still rising toward ~5 kOe) look different

concerns.concern: The paper does not state whether the signal sign matches a Pt/YIG single-crystal reference in the same geometry.
concerns.quote: State whether the signal sign matches that of a Pt/YIG single-crystal reference in the same geometry.

concerns.concern: Pt thicknesses are inferred from deposition time and a single 5 nm TEM calibration. Pt content should be measured directly (ICP or mass gain).
concerns.quote: The 15/30 nm thicknesses are inferred from deposition time, extrapolated from a single 5 nm TEM calibration.

concerns.concern: EDX shows Pt concentrated among fine fragments, and pressing may fracture particles and expose uncoated surfaces. TEM/STEM of the consolidated composite is needed to support claims of continuous Pt channels surrounding YIG grains.
concerns.quote: TEM/STEM of the consolidated composite, not just the as-coated powder, is needed

concerns.concern: All data come from one sample per condition from a single batch, without error bars. Factor-of-two differences between conditions, and the close isotropy agreement, cannot be interpreted.
concerns.quote: Without reproducibility data and error bars on S, σ_eff, and κ, the factor-of-two differences between conditions cannot be interpreted.

concerns.concern: Doubling Pt thickness reduces S by only 15–20% rather than halving it, while conductivity rises superlinearly. Calling this qualitatively consistent with thin films is inadequate.
concerns.quote: Calling this "qualitatively consistent" with thin-film behavior is not adequate.

concerns.concern: The 300 °C samples have roughly half the S of the room-temperature samples. This may be due to interfacial oxidation from pressing in air, which should be investigated (e.g., TEM/EELS).
concerns.quote: interfacial oxidation or reaction lowering the spin-mixing conductance is a plausible cause and should be investigated

concerns.concern: In the Hx-∇zT geometry, the thermal tape's resistance may cause the gradient to be overestimated. Thermocouple locations and sample dimensions should be given, and the in-sample gradient ideally measured directly.
concerns.quote: The tape's thermal resistance may be comparable to that of a low-κ sample, so the gradient could be significantly overestimated.

concerns.concern: Uniaxial pressing likely produces texture, but the orientation of x and z relative to the pressing axis is not stated. Isotropy should be tested on more than one sample and for all permutations relative to the pressing axis.
concerns.quote: The relationship of x and z to the pressing axis must be stated.

concerns.concern: The magnetization units appear mislabeled: plotted ~0.027 "emu/g" for YIG versus ~27 emu/g expected. The quoted 37.9 emu/g is near the 0 K value; this needs correction and reconciliation.
concerns.quote: The axis appears to be in A·m²/g or otherwise mislabeled; please correct and reconcile.

concerns.concern: The "2–3 orders of magnitude" conductivity gain is overstated, since one sample is only ~10× above the reference. Thin-film conductivity can also be raised simply by thickening Pt.
concerns.quote: The "2–3 orders of magnitude" range is generous.

concerns.concern: The very small figure of merit, zT of about 10⁻¹⁰, should be stated explicitly.
concerns.quote: For context, zT ≈ 5 × 10⁻¹³ × 300 / 1.87 ≈ 10⁻¹⁰. This should be stated explicitly.

concerns.concern: A quantitative effective-medium model, including the 1/3 orientational averaging factor, would help explain why S is ~10× below single-crystal values.
concerns.quote: A quantitative effective-medium model would considerably strengthen the paper.

concerns.concern: Possible Joule heating at 100 mA in the Hall measurement and any resulting thermal artifacts are not discussed.
concerns.quote: Comment on Joule heating at 100 mA (~tens of mW for a ~Ω sample) and any resulting thermal artifacts.

concerns.concern: A particle-size distribution is needed. It determines the Pt volume fraction and how grain size compares with the magnon length, since smaller grains reduce SSE.
concerns.quote: provide a particle-size distribution. It determines both the Pt volume fraction (~6t/d) and how grain size compares with λ_m.

concerns.concern: TEM images of the 15 nm and 30 nm coated powders themselves are not shown.
concerns.quote: show TEM of the 15/30 nm powders

concerns.concern: The same PDF card number is given for both FePt and Y₂O₃, so one is wrong.
concerns.quote: The PDF number for FePt (#43-0661) is identical to that given for Y₂O₃. One of them is wrong.

concerns.concern: The weak peak near 29° assigned to Y₂O₃ lies close to YIG (400) and should be checked.
concerns.quote: The assignment of a weak Y₂O₃ peak "near 29°" also sits close to YIG (400) and should be checked.

concerns.concern: Temperature dependence or high-field suppression data characteristic of YIG magnons would further support the SSE assignment (optional).
concerns.quote: Temperature dependence, or high-field suppression characteristic of YIG magnons.

concerns.concern: Attributing low thermal conductivity to YIG/Pt interfacial phonon scattering is speculative. Contact resistance in porous cold-pressed compacts could explain it.
concerns.quote: Attributing the low κ to YIG/Pt interfacial phonon scattering is speculative.

concerns.concern: The introduction wrongly implies S decreases with ferromagnet thickness beyond the magnon length. S is intensive, so the argument should be framed in terms of power factor and power density.
concerns.quote: S = E/∇T is intensive and does not decrease for t_FM > λ_m.

concerns.concern: Prior multilayer, bulk-composite and coating approaches to scaling SSE are not discussed explicitly.
concerns.quote: Prior multilayer, bulk-composite, and coating approaches to scaling the SSE should also be discussed explicitly

concerns.concern: The abstract claims robust mechanical integrity, but no mechanical data are presented.
concerns.quote: No mechanical data are presented; provide some (hardness, flexural strength) or remove the claim.

concerns.concern: The term "bad metal" is misapplied to a percolating composite, and comparisons to undoped Si/Ge are not meaningful. A power-factor comparison with ANE/thermoelectric materials would be more relevant.
concerns.quote: I suggest removing it. Comparisons to undoped Si/Ge are not meaningful here.

concerns.concern: Relative density is computed against pure YIG density. Including Pt raises the theoretical density, so true relative densities are lower.
concerns.quote: Including Pt raises the theoretical density, so true relative densities are lower.

concerns.concern: The 30-RT specific heat exceeds that of single-crystal YIG although Pt should lower it; DSC uncertainty should be discussed.
concerns.quote: Yet 30-RT (0.67 J/gK) exceeds single-crystal YIG; please comment on DSC uncertainty.

concerns.concern: Room-temperature pressing is cold compaction and should not be called sintering.
concerns.quote: Room-temperature pressing is cold compaction, not sintering.

concerns.concern: Units and uncertainties should be given for all S values, and error bars shown in Fig. S5.
concerns.quote: Give units and uncertainties for all S values, and show error bars in Fig. S5.

concerns.concern: On p. 7, the configuration label H_x-∇_zT should read H_z-∇_xT.
concerns.quote: should read H_z-∇_xT

concerns.concern: "Symmetrized" should be "antisymmetrized" for removal of field-even components, in the main text and the Hall Methods.
concerns.quote: "Symmetrized … to remove field-even components" should read *antisymmetrized*

concerns.concern: The Cu-Kα wavelength is inconsistent between Methods and Note S2.
concerns.quote: Cu-Kα wavelength: 0.15406 nm (Methods) vs 0.15418 nm (Note S2).

concerns.concern: Note S2 refers to the XRD figure as Fig. S2 instead of Fig. S3.
concerns.quote: Note S2 refers to XRD as Fig. S2; it is Fig. S3.

concerns.concern: There are spelling errors: "Galosov" should be Golosov, and "worth nothing" should be "worth noting".
concerns.quote: "Galosov" should be Golosov (Note S1). "It is worth nothing" should be "noting" (Methods).

concerns.concern: Author contributions mention VSM, but Methods describe SQUID-MPMS.
concerns.quote: Author contributions mention VSM; Methods describe SQUID-MPMS.

concerns.concern: The Fig. S4 caption misstates which panels contain dashed lines, and the κ references are inconsistently described as literature versus measured values.
concerns.quote: dashed lines are said to appear in panels (b)–(c) but appear in (b), (d), (e).

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3 caption sentence mapping subscripts to ∇T, I and H is confusing.
concerns.quote: the sentence on subscripts (x, y, z ↔ ∇T, I, H) is confusing; please rephrase.

concerns.concern: Author name order is inconsistent with the family-name conventions used elsewhere.
concerns.quote: Author name order: "Hirata Keisuke" vs. family-name conventions elsewhere.
